title: First Word Bismillahs Blessing Through A Comparison And A Warning To The Nafs

questions.question: What is presented as the beginning of every good action?
questions.answer: Saying Allah’s name at the start.

questions.question: Besides being a sign of Islam, what else is said about this blessed phrase?
questions.answer: It is shown as something all creation expresses in its own way.

questions.question: In the comparison, why does a traveler in the desert need to go under a tribal leader’s protection?
questions.answer: So he can be safe from danger and get what he needs.

questions.question: What was the main difference between the two men who entered the desert?
questions.answer: One was humble and accepted protection, while the other was proud and refused it.

questions.question: What happened when the humble man met robbers?
questions.answer: He was left alone because he was traveling under a leader’s name.

questions.question: How was the humble man treated when he reached tents?
questions.answer: People treated him with honor because of the name he carried.

questions.question: What happened to the proud man during the journey?
questions.answer: He faced many troubles, became afraid, begged from others, and was looked down on.

questions.question: In the lesson drawn from the story, who is the traveler and what is the desert?
questions.answer: The human being is the traveler, and this world is the desert.

questions.question: What two human weaknesses are described as having no limit?
questions.answer: Weakness and need.

questions.question: Why should a person take the name of Allah according to the passage?
questions.answer: So he will not fear everything or lower himself by begging from all creation.

questions.question: What does this phrase connect a weak and needy person to?
questions.answer: Allah’s endless power and mercy.

questions.question: How are weakness and need changed when a person says Allah’s name?
questions.answer: They become a means for receiving help and mercy from Allah.

questions.question: What example is given to explain a person who acts in Allah’s name?
questions.answer: A person enrolled in the army who acts with the authority of the government.

questions.question: According to that example, why is such a person not afraid?
questions.answer: Because he acts with lawful authority, not by himself alone.

questions.question: What is one main idea of the whole passage?
questions.answer: Starting with Allah’s name gives protection, strength, and honor.

questions.question: What special phrase is the passage explaining?
questions.answer: The phrase that means beginning in Allah’s name.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the power and blessings connected to this phrase?
questions.answer: They are shown as never running out.

questions.question: What kind of story is used to teach this lesson?
questions.answer: A comparison about traveling through a desert.

questions.question: Why is the desert journey dangerous for someone traveling alone?
questions.answer: Because there are many threats and many needs he cannot handle by himself.

questions.question: Which man made the wiser choice in the story?
questions.answer: The humble man.

questions.question: What wise step did the humble man take before traveling?
questions.answer: He traveled under the name and protection of a chief.

questions.question: What mistake did the proud man make?
questions.answer: He trusted himself and refused protection.

questions.question: How did pride hurt the second man?
questions.answer: It left him scared, needy, and dishonored.

questions.question: What does the passage teach the speaker’s nafs about life in this world?
questions.answer: That it is like a hard journey where a person cannot succeed alone.

questions.question: What feeling can a person leave behind by beginning in Allah’s name?
questions.answer: Constant fear.

questions.question: What shameful behavior can a person avoid by doing that?
questions.answer: Begging from everything around him.

questions.question: What treasure is found in this phrase?
questions.answer: It gives access to Allah’s strength and mercy.

questions.question: In the army example, whose name gives the soldier confidence?
questions.answer: The government’s name.

questions.question: What does the soldier example teach about acting in Allah’s name?
questions.answer: It teaches that a believer gains courage and support by relying on Allah, not just himself.

questions.question: What should Muslims begin with according to the passage?
questions.answer: They should begin with Allah’s name.

questions.question: Why is this phrase called blessed in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it brings goodness, support, and mercy.

questions.question: Where does the comparison in the passage take place?
questions.answer: In the deserts of Arabia.

questions.question: What does a traveler gain by entering under a chief’s protection?
questions.answer: Safety and help in meeting his needs.

questions.question: Which man was described with good character at the start of the story?
questions.answer: The modest and humble man.

questions.question: Which man had a bad attitude, and what was it?
questions.answer: The other man, who was proud and full of himself.

questions.question: What happened to the humble traveler when he used the chief’s name?
questions.answer: People did not harm him, and he received respect.

questions.question: Why did the proud traveler suffer so much?
questions.answer: Because he relied on himself instead of going with protection.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the number of our enemies and needs?
questions.answer: They are too many to count.

questions.question: What should a person do since human weakness and need are so great?
questions.answer: He should rely on Allah by taking His name.

questions.question: How does the phrase help a person before Allah?
questions.answer: It turns his weakness and need into a reason for mercy.

questions.question: What comparison is made between saying Allah’s name and joining the army?
questions.answer: Both mean acting with support from a higher authority.

questions.question: What can a person endure when he acts in Allah’s name?
questions.answer: He can face difficult matters with courage.

questions.question: What lesson about humility can be learned from the two travelers?
questions.answer: Humility brings safety and honor, while pride brings harm and disgrace.

questions.question: What is the first teaching given in this passage?
questions.answer: That every good beginning should be with Allah’s name.

questions.question: What does the passage say this phrase is for Islam?
questions.answer: It is one of its clear signs.

questions.question: What does the story invite the listener to understand about this phrase?
questions.answer: That it gives great strength and many blessings.

questions.question: In the story, what kind of land were the two men crossing?
questions.answer: A desert land.

questions.question: Why would a person be in great danger there without protection?
questions.answer: He would face attacks and many needs by himself.

questions.question: How did the humble traveler show wisdom?
questions.answer: He accepted support instead of depending only on himself.

questions.question: What did the proud traveler’s attitude lead him to do?
questions.answer: It led him to reject protection and go alone.

questions.question: What was the result for the first traveler?
questions.answer: He traveled safely and was treated well.

questions.question: What was the result for the second traveler?
questions.answer: He suffered, feared everything, and lost his dignity.

questions.question: When the passage speaks to the nafs, what truth about a person is being taught?
questions.answer: That a person is weak and needy in this world.

questions.question: What does taking Allah’s name save a person from?
questions.answer: From fear of events and from depending on everything else.

questions.question: What kind of “treasury” is this phrase said to be?
questions.answer: A blessed source of strength and mercy.

questions.question: In what way is a believer like a soldier in the final example?
questions.answer: He acts with the support of a higher authority and is not left alone.

questions.question: What big message ties the story and the final example together?
questions.answer: Relying on Allah brings protection and honor, while trusting only yourself leads to trouble.

questions.question: According to the passage, what should come first in all good things?
questions.answer: Beginning with Allah’s name.

questions.question: What does the passage say all creatures do in their own way?
questions.answer: They point to and declare Allah’s name through how they were made.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the desert story?
questions.answer: To help the reader understand the value of saying Allah’s name.

questions.question: What two problems does a lone traveler face in the desert?
questions.answer: Enemies and needs.

questions.question: What personal quality helped the first man make a good choice?
questions.answer: Humility.

questions.question: What personal quality led the second man to make a bad choice?
questions.answer: Pride.

questions.question: How did using the chief’s name help the first traveler with dangerous people?
questions.answer: It protected him from being attacked.

questions.question: How did it help him with ordinary people in the tents?
questions.answer: It caused them to welcome and honor him.

questions.question: What shows that the proud traveler was inwardly weak?
questions.answer: He was frightened by everything and had to beg.

questions.question: When the lesson is explained, what does the passage call the human self?
questions.answer: A traveler.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about human ability on its own?
questions.answer: It is not enough because people are very weak and needy.

questions.question: What should a person do instead of begging from the universe?
questions.answer: Turn to Allah and act in His name.

questions.question: What makes this phrase like a treasure chest?
questions.answer: It opens the way to endless help and mercy.

questions.question: Why is joining the army a good example here?
questions.answer: Because the soldier has backing, authority, and courage beyond his own strength.

questions.question: What is one strong warning the passage gives through the proud traveler?
questions.answer: Depending on yourself with arrogance leads to fear, hardship, and disgrace.

questions.question: What phrase stands at the center of this passage?
questions.answer: The phrase that means “In the Name of Allah.”

questions.question: How does the passage describe this phrase at the beginning?
questions.answer: As the proper start of every good matter.

questions.question: What else is this phrase described as in relation to Islam?
questions.answer: A mark or sign of Islam.

questions.question: What teaching method is used after the introduction?
questions.answer: A story that compares life to a desert journey.

questions.question: What did travelers in that setting need from a tribal leader?
questions.answer: His name and protection.

questions.question: Why was that protection so important?
questions.answer: It helped them survive attacks and get what they needed.

questions.question: How were the two men different in character?
questions.answer: One was humble, and the other was arrogant.

questions.question: What did the humble man do that the proud man refused to do?
questions.answer: He traveled under a leader’s name.

questions.question: How did this choice affect the humble man’s journey?
questions.answer: It made his path safer and brought him respect.

questions.question: How did the proud man’s choice affect his journey?
questions.answer: It filled his trip with trouble, fear, and humiliation.

questions.question: In the lesson after the story, what do “endless enemies and needs” help us understand?
questions.answer: They show how much a person needs Allah’s help in this world.

questions.question: Who should a person rely on, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Allah, the eternal Lord.

questions.question: What does the passage say this phrase gives to someone who feels powerless?
questions.answer: A connection to Allah’s unlimited power and mercy.

questions.question: How can weakness and poverty become something good in this teaching?
questions.answer: They can lead a person to seek Allah sincerely and receive His mercy.

questions.question: What final picture explains how a believer can act bravely?
questions.answer: The picture of a soldier acting with the authority of the state.
